Topic: The Geometry of High-Dimensional Spheres: Beyond the 3rd Dimension

Target audience: University students (STEM majors)

Section: section_1 — Prerequisite Review: Scaling Intuition

Lecture lines:
Radius, area, and volume scale as powers.
Dimensions define our spatial boundaries.
Unit spheres exist in any dimension.
Visualizing hypercubes shows growth.
Scaling intuition guides our journey.

Planned animations:
Fade in unit square with side length 1, colored #FFFFFF.
Increase side length to 2, square scales up to area 4, colored #FFFF00.
Contrast volume increase in 3D: cube expands to volume 8, colored #00FFFF.

Section: section_2 — The Curse of Dimensionality: Volume Concentration

Lecture lines:
Volume hides near the outer shell.
Imagine spheres as nested onion layers.
The bulk mass drifts outward.
Center space remains effectively empty.
Robot scouts confirm the hollow interior.

Planned animations:
Display unit hypercube in high dimensions.
Highlight shell area with color #FF00FF.
Shrink inner volume to show concentration, color #FFA500.
Draw distribution density curve showing peaks at boundaries.
Animate flow outward to illustrate concentration, color #00FF00.

Section: section_3 — The Shrinking Sphere Paradox

Lecture lines:
Fixed radius spheres shrink in higher dimensions.
Volume approaches zero as dimensions grow.
High-dimensional space becomes magically hollow.

Planned animations:
Draw unit hypersphere in 2D, colored #FFFFFF.
Project sphere into higher dimensions while showing shrinking volume fraction.
Animate radius relative to box, using #FF4500 to highlight discrepancy.
Simulate particle distribution falling outside the hypersphere, #8A2BE2.
Show final ratio converging to zero, color #FFD700.

Section: section_4 — Visualizing the Corners

Lecture lines:
Spheres reside inside hypercubes.
Corners stretch far from the center.
Distance to corners grows exponentially.

Planned animations:
Display 2D square corners, labeled A, B, C, D in #FFFFFF.
Add dimension 3 showing 8 corners, flashing #FFFF00.
Demonstrate exponential growth of corners with dimension increase.
Color corners using #00FFFF to highlight extremity positions.
Show path connecting corners to illustrate space sparseness.

Section: section_5 — Summary & Real-World Application

Lecture lines:
High-dimensional space is spiky and empty.
Data points behave like isolated stars.
Empty space challenges machine learning algorithms.

Planned animations:
List key concepts: Scaling, Concentration, Sparseness in #FFFFFF.
Show data point spread across feature space, color #00FF00.
Fade out all elements to black #000000.

        # BASE

        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")

        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")

                y = 2.2 - i * 1

        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]

        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

class TeachingScene(Scene):
